item.text: {"search_note":"I found no strong 2024 evidence that Abiy materially strengthened the underlying democratic system enough to offset the repression. The positive items are procedural and limited to selected elections and reform claims; they do not outweigh the broader pattern of emergency rule, intimidation, and restrictions on opposition, media, and online access.","evidence":[{"title":"Freedom in the World 2025: Ethiopia","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2025","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-world/2025","summary":"Freedom House says Abiy-era electoral-law and NEBE reforms improved electoral operations, and that some June 2024 legislative/regional elections were peaceful and credible according to AU observers. This is the best positive evidence for procedural continuity, but it is narrow and does not show broad democratic strengthening.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.8","4B.2","4B.4"]},{"title":"Final Observation Report on the June 24, 2024 reruns","publisher":"CECOE","date":"2024","url":"https://cecoe.org/download/final-observation-report-on-the-outstanding-and-reelections-of-the-sixth-general-elections-held-in-benishangul-gumuz-afar-somali-and-central-ethiopia-regions-in-june-24-2024/","summary":"Domestic observers described the June 24 rerun elections as transparent enough for systematic observation, with broad observer deployment and monitoring of polling, counting, and the post-election environment. This supports a narrow positive reading on electoral procedure, not a general strengthening of democracy.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.8","4B.4"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Ethiopia","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-01-12","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia","summary":"HRW said authorities restricted social media, arrested opposition figures and journalists, and used emergency powers in ways that narrowed political space. It also noted that fighting and repression left opposition groups with little meaningful room to participate. This is strong evidence that democratic resilience weakened.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.8","4B.7","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/","summary":"Amnesty said the state of emergency was used to silence dissent through warrantless arrests, movement limits, bans on assemblies, and arrests of politicians and journalists. This is direct evidence of declining political freedom under emergency rule.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.8","4B.7","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Journalist arrested under state of emergency: Belay Manaye","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-03-14","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/afr25/7782/2024/en/","summary":"Amnesty reports Belay Manaye was arrested by police and security personnel, held without being told the reason, and believed detained for reporting on the Amhara conflict; it also says other journalists were arrested under the emergency. This is direct evidence of repression of criticism and worsening democratic space.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"Ethiopia: Internet Freedom","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/ethiopia/freedom-net/2024","summary":"Freedom House says authorities restricted mobile internet in Amhara, disrupted mobile internet during fighting, restricted social media in early February after protests in Oromia, and used the state of emergency to curtail online expression and detain journalists without charge. This is strong evidence that digital controls were used to weaken political freedom.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.6","4B.5"]},{"title":"The state-of-emergency proclamation centralized coercive authority","publisher":"ENA English","date":"2024-11-03","url":"https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124","summary":"The proclamation centralized coercive authority under an operation command, allowed replacement of local administrators, restricted CSOs and media suspected of aiding “terrorist” groups, imposed ID and movement controls, and suspended normal judicial handling of enforcement. This is a strong sign of institutional weakening, not resilience.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.8","4B.7","4B.6","4B.5","4B.4"]},{"title":"Authorities suspended three rights groups while Abiy praised reforms","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-12-02","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups","summary":"HRW said the government suspended three rights groups while Abiy publicly praised reforms like media freedom and NGO registration. The operational pattern is selective punishment of civic actors, not strengthening of democratic resilience.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.9","4B.7","4B.6","4B.5","4B.4"]},{"title":"Secret security committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels","publisher":"Reuters via EHRC","date":"2024-02-27","url":"https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/","summary":"Reuters, via the EHRC, reported a secret “Koree Nageenyaa” committee that interfered in the justice system and was linked to widespread human-rights violations. This is evidence of extra-constitutional coercive power, which undercuts democratic resilience.","question_ids":["4B.10","4B.8","4B.5","4B.4","4B.9"]}]}
